title_en: The Limb of the Brahmajnani (the Knower of the Formless Brahman)
translit:
|| Ath Shri Brahmajnanika Ang ||21||

Sitapati Raghunath bin | ko kahuko dhariye dhyan ||
Dhua dharhar jyun Jivana | aiso brahmajnan ||1||
Sitapati taj Jivana | rahyo Brahmasu lag ||
Rui mandirmen paith kar | dvare lagai ag ||2||
Sitapati taj Jivana | dhyan dhare akash ||
Pragat godko chhandke | kare garbhki ash ||3||
Pragat Harijan chhandke | dhyan dhare akash ||
Ve jan jug jug Jivana | Ravisutke nij das ||4||
Brahmajnani anusare | ghat ghat vyapak Ram ||
Hamare yun vrat Jivana | je Sitapatiko nam ||5||
Bud panth sab Jivana | jap tap tirath dan ||
Sitapatikun tyagke | je kathe brahmajnan ||6||
Trikuti sanjam Jivana | Brahm jot prakash ||
Sitapati Raghunath bin | svarg narkman vas ||7||
Adhyatam vidya unmuni | kare so kotha khol ||
Ramnam bin Jivana | e sab jamka kol ||8||
Mul dvare edi dai | pavan valove akash ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | svarg nark manhi vas ||9||
Ingla pingla sukhmana | ravi shashi donun mel ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | jamsun karvo kel ||10||
Ashtadal kamal je koi jape | koi dhyan dhare akash ||
Bhaj Sitapati Jivana | Lakshmi charan nivas ||11||
Ankh michine andhlo | dhyan dhare akash ||
Sitapati bhutal Jivana | jahan sant sangat nivas ||12||
Gadhe linde Jivana | papad pitho thay ||
To andevne anusari | jagat mukti fal pay ||13||
Jugat bani e Jivana | sab ho baithe sadh ||
Ape ap thadhe bhaye | janam gamayo bad ||14||
Ghat ghatman Hari lekhve | ape ho rahyo Brahm ||
Mide hato Jivana | te shir par lino karm ||15||
Jyun jalmen pratibimb hai | tyun ghat ghat vyapak Ram ||
Guru prasade Jivana | paie mul chandrako dham ||16||
Sainya seti Jivana | kabahun na kije rosh ||
Ape ghat ghat le rahyo | ape banayo ghosh ||17||
Shruti smriti kahe Jivana | raho nam sharan vishvas ||
Apmate uthayke | bhavjal dube das ||18||
Ghat ghat to Hari janiye | pan Sainya santo pas ||
Dhua dharhar Jivana | tame kaiso vas ||19||
Jan jane Hariki gati | Hari jane janki ghat ||
Aras paras e Jivana | or na duji bat ||20||
Vishva pokhan Hari sabe kare | or vishva pokhe sabe ap ||
Aise vyapak Jivana | kyon mite tretap ||21||
Sain lahe sab jivki | Sainki lahe na koy ||
Sainki lahe je Jivana | jake sant samagam hoy ||22||

|| Iti Shri Brahmajnanika Ang sampurna ||21||
|| Iti Shri pancham vishram sampurna ||
|| Iti Shri Jivanji Maharajni sakhio sampurna ||
translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Brahmajnani (the claimant to knowledge of the formless Brahman), 21.

1. Apart from Sitapati Raghunath (Ram, the lord of Sita), on whom is one to fix meditation? Like a mansion built of smoke, O Jivana - such is that brahmajnan.

2. Forsaking Sitapati, O Jivana, he has fastened himself upon the formless Brahman; it is like entering a house of cotton and setting a fire at its door.

3. Forsaking Sitapati, O Jivana, he fixes his meditation upon the empty sky; he leaves the lap that is plainly there and longs for the womb again.

4. Leaving the manifest harijans (devotees of Hari), he fixes his meditation upon the sky; such men, age after age, O Jivana, are the very servants of the sun's son (Yama, the lord of death).

5. The brahmajnani follows after "Ram pervading every heart"; our vow, O Jivana, is this - the name of Sitapati.

6. All those paths are drowned, O Jivana - japa (repetition), austerity, pilgrimage, charity - where a man forsakes Sitapati and expounds brahmajnan.

7. The trikuti (the point between the brows), the disciplines, the blaze of Brahman's light, O Jivana - without Sitapati Raghunath they end only in a dwelling in heaven or hell.

8. Spiritual lore and the unmuni trance, by which he throws open chamber after chamber within - without the name of Ram, O Jivana, all of it is a bargain struck with death.

9. Pressing the heel against the root-gate, he churns the breath up into the sky; without Sitapati, O Jivana, it is a dwelling in heaven or hell.

10. Ingla, pingla and sushumna, the joining of both sun and moon - without Sitapati, O Jivana, it is playing games with death.

11. Some repeat the mantra on the eight-petalled lotus, some fix meditation on the sky; worship Sitapati, O Jivana, at whose feet Lakshmi dwells.

12. Shutting his eyes, the blind man fixes his meditation on the sky; Sitapati is here on the face of the earth, O Jivana, where the company of the saints abides.

13. If out of donkey-dung, O Jivana, papad-flour could be made, then indeed the world would get the fruit of liberation by following other gods.

14. This is the contrivance now, O Jivana: everyone has sat himself down as a sadhu; of their own accord they have set themselves up, and have wasted their birth for nothing.

15. He reckons Hari to be in every heart and takes himself to have become Brahman; he was a mere cipher, O Jivana, and has taken karma upon his own head.

16. As a reflection lies in water, so does Ram pervade every heart; by the Guru's grace, O Jivana, one attains the abode of the original Moon.

17. With the Lord, O Jivana, never be angry; He Himself has taken up residence in every heart, and He Himself has made all this clamour.

18. Shruti and Smriti say, O Jivana: abide in the refuge of the Name with faith; rising up in his own self-will, the servant drowns in the ocean of existence.

19. Hari is indeed to be known in every heart, but the Lord is present beside the saints; a mansion of smoke, O Jivana - what dwelling can there be in that?

20. The devotee knows the ways of Hari, and Hari knows the inmost turn of the devotee; it is mutual, O Jivana - there is no second matter to it.

21. Hari does all the nourishing of the universe, and the universe in turn nourishes Him; by such a pervading alone, O Jivana, how shall the threefold affliction be removed?

22. The Lord knows the state of every living being, but no one knows the Lord's; he alone comes to know the Lord, O Jivana, who has the company of the saints.

|| Here ends the Limb of the Brahmajnani, 21. ||
|| Here ends the fifth Vishram (rest-section). ||
|| Here end the sakhis (couplets) of Jivanji Maharaj. ||
